papers.title: TranscriptFormer: A generative cell atlas across 1.5 billion years of evolution
papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics is revolutionizing our understanding of cellular diversity, yet comparing transcriptional programs across the tree of life remains challenging. We developed TranscriptFormer, a family of generative foundation models trained on up to 112 million cells spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution across 12 species. We demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on cell type classification, even for species separated over 685 million years of evolution, and zero-shot disease state identification in human cells. Developmental trajectories, phylogenetic relationships and cellular hierarchies emerge naturally in TranscriptFormer's representations without any explicit training on these annotations. This work establishes a powerful framework for quantitative single-cell analysis and comparative cellular biology, thus demonstrating that universal principles of cellular organization can be learned and predicted across the tree of life.

我们在细胞类型分类方面展现了顶尖的性能，即便是那些在进化过程中相隔超过6.85亿年的物种也不例外；同时，我们还在人类细胞的疾病状态识别领域实现了零样本学习能力。
在 TranscriptFormer的表示体系中，发育轨迹、系统发育关系以及细胞层级结构会自然而然地显现出来，而无需对这些注释进行任何显式的训练。

papers.title: 3DICE: Interpretable 3D Cross-Modal Learning for Drug–Target Interaction Prediction and Large-Scale Drug Discovery
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug–target interaction (DTI) prediction is a crucial step in modern drug discovery. Accurate and efficient predictions can substantially reduce costs and development time. Applications of deep learning methods for this purpose have been extensively studied in recent years, yielding instrumental contributions to this field. However, existing methods face issues pertaining to efficient learning of drug and target feature representations, which is detrimental to generalisability and performance in cold-start scenarios. Most approaches extract representations from SMILES strings for drugs and FASTA sequences for target proteins, which encode limited 3D structural information. Additionally, many models lack explainability, being black boxes that provide little physical insight into the underlying mechanisms behind such interactions. Results We propose 3DICE, a novel framework leveraging co-attention-based fusion and massively pre-trained 3D structural encoders for both drugs and proteins. Uni-Mol and ESM-IF1 are employed to generate high-fidelity, 3D structure-aware embeddings which enable richer geometric and chemical understanding. Cross-modal fusion modules further augment representations to model intermolecular binding relationships. Importantly, this mechanism also provides intrinsic interpretability, highlighting and enabling qualitative analysis of most influential atoms or residues. Experiments conducted on two canonical benchmark datasets display the competitiveness of our model in real-world scenarios. 3DICE outperformed state-of-the-art models across multiple metrics on the DrugBank and KIBA datasets. Additional experiments provide a more rigorous analysis of interpretability than is typically reported in prior DTI studies, and we find that attention consistently highlights decision-critical regions which is not intrinsically class-specific. Availability Our model and dataset are freely available at: https://github.com/austinatose/3DICE

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
药物-靶标相互作用预测是现代药物发现过程中的关键步骤。准确高效的预测方法能够显著降低研发成本与时间。近年来，深度学习技术在这一领域得到了广泛研究，并为该领域的发展做出了重要贡献。然而，现有方法在高效提取药物与靶标的特征表示方面仍存在不足，这限制了这些模型的泛化能力及在全新数据场景下的表现。目前大多数方法都是从药物的SMILES字符串或靶标蛋白质的FASTA序列中提取特征表示，而这些信息仅能编码有限的3D结构信息。此外，许多模型缺乏可解释性，本质上属于“黑箱”，无法为人们提供关于这些相互作用机制的物理层面的理解。  

**研究内容**  
我们提出了3DICE这一新型框架，该框架结合了基于协同注意力的特征融合技术以及针对药物和蛋白质预先训练好的3D结构编码器，能够生成高保真度、具备3D结构信息的特征表示。其中，Uni-Mol与ESM-IF1算法被用于生成这种特征表示，从而实现更深入的几何与化学层面的分析；跨模态融合模块进一步增强了这些特征表示的能力，有助于模拟分子间的结合关系。更重要的是，这一框架具有内在的可解释性，能够明确指出那些对药物-靶标相互作用起关键作用的原子或残基，从而便于进行定性分析。在两个标准基准数据集上进行的实验表明，我们的模型在现实应用中具备较强的竞争力——在DrugBank与KIBA数据集上，3DICE在多项评估指标上的表现均优于现有最先进模型。进一步的可解释性分析也证实，注意力机制始终能够有效识别出那些对预测结果起决定性作用的区域，且这种能力并不依赖于具体的分子类型。  

**模型与数据集的公开方式**  
我们的模型及相关数据集已免费开放在以下链接中：  
https://github.com/austinatose/3DICE

all_papers.title: TranscriptFormer: A generative cell atlas across 1.5 billion years of evolution
all_papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics is revolutionizing our understanding of cellular diversity, yet comparing transcriptional programs across the tree of life remains challenging. We developed TranscriptFormer, a family of generative foundation models trained on up to 112 million cells spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution across 12 species. We demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on cell type classification, even for species separated over 685 million years of evolution, and zero-shot disease state identification in human cells. Developmental trajectories, phylogenetic relationships and cellular hierarchies emerge naturally in TranscriptFormer's representations without any explicit training on these annotations. This work establishes a powerful framework for quantitative single-cell analysis and comparative cellular biology, thus demonstrating that universal principles of cellular organization can be learned and predicted across the tree of life.

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Single-cell transcriptomics is revolutionizing our understanding of cellular diversity, yet comparing transcriptional programs across the tree of life remains challenging. We developed TranscriptFormer, a family of generative foundation models trained on up to 112 million cells spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution across 12 species. We demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on cell type classification, even for species separated over 685 million years of evolution, and zero-shot disease state identification in human cells. Developmental trajectories, phylogenetic relationships and cellular hierarchies emerge naturally in TranscriptFormer's representations without any explicit training on these annotations. This work establishes a powerful framework for quantitative single-cell analysis and comparative cellular biology, thus demonstrating that universal principles of cellular organization can be learned and predicted across the tree of life.

all_papers.title: 3DICE: Interpretable 3D Cross-Modal Learning for Drug–Target Interaction Prediction and Large-Scale Drug Discovery
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug–target interaction (DTI) prediction is a crucial step in modern drug discovery. Accurate and efficient predictions can substantially reduce costs and development time. Applications of deep learning methods for this purpose have been extensively studied in recent years, yielding instrumental contributions to this field. However, existing methods face issues pertaining to efficient learning of drug and target feature representations, which is detrimental to generalisability and performance in cold-start scenarios. Most approaches extract representations from SMILES strings for drugs and FASTA sequences for target proteins, which encode limited 3D structural information. Additionally, many models lack explainability, being black boxes that provide little physical insight into the underlying mechanisms behind such interactions. Results We propose 3DICE, a novel framework leveraging co-attention-based fusion and massively pre-trained 3D structural encoders for both drugs and proteins. Uni-Mol and ESM-IF1 are employed to generate high-fidelity, 3D structure-aware embeddings which enable richer geometric and chemical understanding. Cross-modal fusion modules further augment representations to model intermolecular binding relationships. Importantly, this mechanism also provides intrinsic interpretability, highlighting and enabling qualitative analysis of most influential atoms or residues. Experiments conducted on two canonical benchmark datasets display the competitiveness of our model in real-world scenarios. 3DICE outperformed state-of-the-art models across multiple metrics on the DrugBank and KIBA datasets. Additional experiments provide a more rigorous analysis of interpretability than is typically reported in prior DTI studies, and we find that attention consistently highlights decision-critical regions which is not intrinsically class-specific. Availability Our model and dataset are freely available at: https://github.com/austinatose/3DICE

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
药物-靶标相互作用预测是现代药物发现过程中的关键步骤。准确高效的预测方法能够显著降低研发成本与时间。近年来，深度学习技术在这一领域得到了广泛研究，并为该领域的发展做出了重要贡献。然而，现有方法在高效提取药物与靶标的特征表示方面仍存在不足，这限制了这些模型的泛化能力及在全新数据场景下的表现。目前大多数方法都是从药物的SMILES字符串或靶标蛋白质的FASTA序列中提取特征表示，而这些信息仅能编码有限的3D结构信息。此外，许多模型缺乏可解释性，本质上属于“黑箱”，无法为人们提供关于这些相互作用机制的物理层面的理解。  

**研究内容**  
我们提出了3DICE这一新型框架，该框架结合了基于协同注意力的特征融合技术以及针对药物和蛋白质预先训练好的3D结构编码器，能够生成高保真度、具备3D结构信息的特征表示。其中，Uni-Mol与ESM-IF1算法被用于生成这种特征表示，从而实现更深入的几何与化学层面的分析；跨模态融合模块进一步增强了这些特征表示的能力，有助于模拟分子间的结合关系。更重要的是，这一框架具有内在的可解释性，能够明确指出那些对药物-靶标相互作用起关键作用的原子或残基，从而便于进行定性分析。在两个标准基准数据集上进行的实验表明，我们的模型在现实应用中具备较强的竞争力——在DrugBank与KIBA数据集上，3DICE在多项评估指标上的表现均优于现有最先进模型。进一步的可解释性分析也证实，注意力机制始终能够有效识别出那些对预测结果起决定性作用的区域，且这种能力并不依赖于具体的分子类型。  

**模型与数据集的公开方式**

https://github.com/austinatose/3DICE
